gloss: getting caught up in; collateral damage

definitions.gloss: getting caught up in; getting splashed; collateral damage
definitions.explanation: Suffering unintended negative consequences from someone else's actions or a situation one wasn't directly involved in.

examples.japanese: とばっちりを{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I got caught up in it.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}の{機嫌|きげん}が{悪|わる}くて、とばっちりを{食|く}らった。
examples.english: My boss was in a bad mood and I got caught in the crossfire.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}の{喧嘩|けんか}のとばっちりで{怒|おこ}られた。
examples.english: I got scolded as collateral damage from my friends' fight.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Related to {飛|と}ぶ (to fly) and ちる (to scatter) - originally referring to water splashing on a bystander. Now used metaphorically.

USAGE:
Describes being an innocent victim who suffers due to:
・Others' conflicts or mistakes
・Bad timing or being in the wrong place
・Chain reactions of negative events

COLLOCATIONS:
・とばっちりを{受|う}ける - to receive collateral damage
・とばっちりを{食|く}らう - to get caught up in (stronger)
・とばっちりが{来|く}る - collateral damage comes

REGISTER:
Casual, spoken Japanese. Often used humorously or with mild complaint.
